numbers.source: Wikipedia 'Pallet' (read raw, 13 Oct): the standard European sizes 1200 x 1000 (EUR 2) and 1000 x 1200 (EUR 3) and their 144 mm height; P1's pallet is the 1000 x 1200 kind (boards 1200, stringers 1000: the board length is 1.2 times the width in the photograph)
P1 board width over pitch 0.545 mean (0.59, 0.53, 0.53, 0.53 over five boards: the near boards are nearer the camera) at the 152.5 pitch that 7 boards on 1000 give: 83 mm; 85 chosen (+-6)
7 boards of 85 across 1000 leave 6 gaps of 67.5; pitch 152.5
EUR pallet: boards 22 each, stringers 100 (the 144 total)

numbers.what: the middle stringer's centre from the pallet's centre
numbers.source: P1: the middle cross member of the leaning pallet sits at 345 to 390 px of a 345 px board length: its centre at 0.49 of the board length (+-0.03)

sources.author: Brian Robert Marshall
sources.shows: three timber pallets standing on their long edges against a wall beside a doorway on a paved pavement, one leaning about 12 degrees with seven deck boards seen from the front and three cross members (stringers) between; beside them a stack of plastic fish boxes carrying real firms' names
sources.not_used_for: any absolute size (no scale object); the fish boxes and their lettering (masked); the plastic crates
sources.period: 2011; a softwood stringer pallet is the same object in 1990

sources.author: Jonathan Billinger
sources.shows: heaps of old pallets in an outhouse yard: the edges of stacked pallets show a bottom board, stringer blocks and a top board; boards split and grey
sources.period: 2013, old pallets of the 1980s and 1990s kind

photo_ratio.method: five deck boards on a band of rows 296 to 304 of the 1024 px copy, each edge found by the grey-level step in a window of +-4 px; ratio of board width to pitch is the number a perspective view cannot change much: the camera is to the right so the near (right) boards are drawn larger (the pitch grows 30 to 36 px) but the ratio holds within 0.06

night.note: the yard mouth is between lamp pools; the pallets read as pale vertical slats catching the lantern colour (1, 0.25, 0) on their weathered faces and black in the gaps

placement.slot: west side, in the yard mouth (x 21 to 24), behind the crowd-control barrier the scene puts across it: the leaning pallet against the gable end of the west_south block (its wall face at x 21.0, facing +x), centred at z -6.2; one pallet flat on the yard floor in front of its foot (street x 21.13 to 22.33)
placement.local_to_street: local +y points into the gable wall (street -x); local x runs across the yard mouth (street z)
reasons: the scene's story is that the yard is shut (a barrier across the mouth, cones, a skip): the pallets behind the barrier are the yard's stuff, one event with the skip; the 2 October ruling took the pallet off the street until real, and this target is the 'real' (RULINGS 2 Oct): a decision for DECISIONS, not a question
the earlier slot (x 21.8 on the west pavement, a flat slab) is dropped: a flat pallet on the footway read as a slab; leaning on a wall it reads as a pallet (S1)

the scene's two wooden crates stand on the pavement at z -4.3 (far edges at -4.76), the pallets inside the yard from z -5.7: 0.94 m clear; the self-check reads the crates' places from the scene and measures the clearance
the scene's large_pallet (2.00 x 1.10) is not a British pallet and is not used

wear: boards: weathered grey-brown on the faces, paler at freshly broken or sawn ends; one board split along 400 mm; one board missing on the flat pallet's top deck (a gap of 85 mm: a seed), edges rounded by use and grey with grime on the underside
nail heads (not modelled) rust-stained with a 15 mm brown halo; a few sawn-off nail stubs standing 3 mm proud
damp green stain along the lowest 120 mm of the leaning pallet and on the flat pallet's bottom boards; wet-street darkening on everything below 150 mm
NOT shown: any owner's brand, any stamp, any hire company's colour (a real pallet carries marks; this one is plain)

disagreements.photo: S1: leaning on a wall beside a door
disagreements.chose: leaning on the gable wall in the yard mouth, one flat at its foot

variants_note: PA3 (the sample): one flat, one leaning on the gable wall.
PA1: a single flat pallet (for the loading aprons and the chandler's).
conditions (materials and seeds): C0 new and pale (a few), C1 weathered (the sample), C2 one board broken and one missing. A leaning pallet's lean is 10 to 14 degrees by seed.
not_settled: absolute size: S1 has no scale object, so the 1000 x 1200 x 144 is the European standard (Read), supported by S1's proportions (board length to width of the pallet 1.2), not measured
the board width (85 mm, error 6) comes from a ratio on a perspective view
whether pallets of 1990 were mostly hire pallets with owners' marks (they were; the target leaves every mark off)
the exact yard-mouth clearance: it depends on the crates' places at x 22.4 and 23.1 and the barrier at 22.5, which the scene owns
content_rule_note: no person, no drink, no betting: plain timber (a statement of the content rule).
builder_notes: one mesh per pallet by script: 7 + 3 boards and 3 stringers, boards arrised 1 mm, ends chamfered 15 on the underside; the nails are texture
the leaning pallet is the flat one rotated 78 degrees about its stringer axis (x) with its lowest edge on the ground; the transform is in the part xf of target.json
the gable wall in PA3 is a stand-in: the street's own wall carries the contact
no mark of any kind on any board
